text:
A working fitness app with an optional
AI Coach built around the user’s own log.
Product image: demonstration account, captured 3 August 2026. UI has since evolved.

People who already lift
and track what they eat.
They have a routine. The opportunity is to make daily logging and weekly decisions easier to keep up.
Keep workouts and food in one usable record.
Understand what changed before adjusting training or nutrition.
Proposed customer focus. Customer interviews, cohort retention and willingness to pay remain to be validated.
A working product across the daily routine
Actual OneRep demo-account captures from 3 August 2026. Illustrative account values, not customer outcomes.
Coach can use training, food and goals rather than asking users to reconstruct their history.
Supported actions can create workouts or food records through an approval flow.
AI sharing is opt-in. Core tracking works without Coach, and users can export their data.
Implemented product capabilities. Demo screenshot: 3 August 2026. No claim of clinical effectiveness or improved outcomes.
A large category, a narrow starting point
HFA also reports that free weights led equipment usage growth since 2021.
Self-directed adults who combine strength training with regular food tracking.
How many of these users will switch, stay active and pay for Coach.
Source: HFA, 2026 US Health & Fitness Consumer Report. US membership includes ages 6+. Category context, not OneRep’s addressable market.
Workout logging, routines and a fitness community.
Workout tracking alone must meet a high usability bar.
Nutrition and workout apps, with a combined subscription.
Combining training and food is already a competitive category.
Free core tracking, a shared account and optional AI actions.
The proposed advantage is less logging friction and more useful context.
Retention and useful coaching will determine whether users switch.
Sources: Hevy official site; MacroFactor Workouts and pricing pages; OneRep product and code. Competitive position remains a hypothesis.

Workout, nutrition and progress tracking.
10 AI requests per month.
At 1,000 paying subscribers: €4,990 in monthly gross billings.
Illustrative arithmetic, not a forecast. Before taxes, fees, AI, hosting and support costs. Published web offer; regional store prices may vary.
A working product, an early commercial stage
Web app available. iOS in TestFlight beta, with the App Store release still pending.
Reliable checkout, repeat weekly use and the first paid renewals.
Current focus: establish repeat use, subscription conversion and paid renewals.

Start with small cohorts.
Learn before buying reach.
Invite lifters through relevant communities and coach-led introductions. Offer hands-on onboarding.
Use the existing exercise library and practical training content to reach people with a specific need.
Planned experiments, not established channels or partnerships. Measure activation, four-week retention and conversion by acquisition source.
The milestones that justify the next stage
Complete subscription purchase validation and the iOS release. Make the first workout and food log straightforward.
Measure who returns to both training and nutrition after four weeks, and learn why others stop.
Reach first paid renewals and measure AI cost per paying subscriber alongside support and platform fees.
Compare cohort quality by channel before committing to a larger acquisition budget.
Milestones and priorities are proposed. Fundraising amount, runway, valuation and hiring plan require a separate founder discussion.

A working product.
Paid demand is the next proof.

Seeking investor conversations about the path
to retained users and repeat paid subscriptions.
OneRep website, product source and published pricing. Accessed 20 September 2026.
OneRep reports zero paying subscribers as of 20 September 2026.
Repository demo-account captures dated 3 August 2026. Screens show demonstration data and an earlier UI.
HFA, “81 Million Americans Were Members of a Fitness Facility in 2025,” 9 April 2026.
Hevy (hevyapp.com). MacroFactor Workouts and pricing (macrofactor.com/workouts/price). Accessed 20 September 2026.
Public source uses PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Self-hosting and source availability are distinct from unrestricted commercial use.
Plans and scenario arithmetic are explicitly labeled. Founder background, financing terms and audited operating metrics are outside this introduction.
